title: One red main, one fixer
goal: Give every red build a fingerprint of its problem, so that all the builds that are red for the same reason join one fixer run, and builds with different problems never share one.

guess.q: Main went red because of one broken test, and then 5 people pushed. All 5 builds fail on that same test. If the fixer's workflow ID is cifix:fcp:<hash of the whole failure record>, how many fixer runs start?

options.text: 1, because it is the same problem.
options.why: The record also holds the run id, the start time and the pushed commit, and they change on every build, so the 5 hashes are all different.
Every record is a little different, so every hash is different, and Temporal sees 5 different IDs: a storm of fixers.

options.text: 0, because Temporal refuses to start the same thing twice.
options.why: Temporal only joins or refuses runs with the same ID. These 5 IDs are different, so to Temporal they are 5 different things.

build: Open fingerprint.mjs and write three small functions. firstError(log) gives back the first line that says error or fail. normalise(line) removes what changes on every run: timestamps (in both formats), temp folders like /tmp/ci-8sK2pq, and durations like 48ms or 1.2s. fingerprint(failure) hashes lastGreenSha plus one line per failing job, "job name | normalised first error", sorted, and gives back the first 12 hex characters. Run node storm.mjs until it says 7 red builds on main → 3 fixer runs, then run ./academy check, which also tries 3 red builds you have not seen.
fix: Last night someone wanted "more precise" fixers, so they added the pushed commit to the fingerprint. This morning main went red, ten people pushed, and ten fixer runs started on the same broken test, each one with its own PR. Run node storm.mjs --fix to see the storm, then repair fix/fingerprint.mjs.
explain: Why does the fixer's workflow ID come from a fingerprint of the problem, and not from the build that failed?
Name two things you strip before hashing and two things you keep. Why does each one belong on its side?
Main turned green again, and an hour later the same test broke again. Should that start a new fixer, or join the old one? Why?
done: node storm.mjs shows 7 red builds on main → 3 fixer runs, and ./academy check passes, also on the hidden builds.
